verdict.rationale: Pulumi's own docs show some bulk-style capability. `pulumi preview --import-file` generates an import file listing every resource a program would create, and policies apply guardrails consistently across all resources. Its code-first model also lets loops define many resources at once, and users report managing environments of about 500 resources. However, no dedicated bulk-operation feature (such as batch update or delete across stacks or resources) is documented as such. Automation API is only a building block for orchestrating many stacks, so it earns no credit here. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented bulk or batch operation command across many stacks or resources, a documented bulk import workflow end-to-end, and hands-on corroboration of bulk operations at scale.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: run `pulumi preview --import-file` to generate an import file listing every resource the program would otherwise create
use standard language features like loops, functions, classes, and package management
You define guardrails in code and apply them consistently across resources managed by Pulumi IaC
